subjects.name: Motion Picture Alliance for the Preservation of American Ideals

summary: Biography of Hollywood cowboy star John Wayne (1907-1979), who avoided service in World War II, abused women, voiced open racism, and used his films, notably The Green Berets, to sell the Vietnam War and a violent ideal of white Christian manhood.

evidence.note: Born Marion Robert Morrison in Winterset, Iowa, 1907
First starring role in The Big Trail, shot drunk and sick in Yuma
Long background on muscular Christianity framing Wayne as its avatar
Account of Wayne punching Marlene Dietrich on set; pattern of hitting women
Affair with teenage Chata begins in Mexico; Mexican yacht trips with Ford's circle
Extended segment on Wayne dodging WWII service while peers enlisted
Helps found and leads the anticommunist Motion Picture Alliance during the Red Scare
The Conqueror shot downwind of Nevada nuclear tests; cast cancer cluster
Pentagon gets script control of The Green Berets in exchange for gear
Wayne tours front lines in Vietnam; film used to drive enlistment
1971 Playboy interview endorsing white supremacy and Native dispossession
Death in 1979, then legacy with Reagan, Buchanan, Gingrich and evangelicals

notes: No theme for masculinity ideals; misogyny-manosphere is the nearest fit for the story's framing of Wayne as a model of toxic manhood. Turn-of-century Roosevelt and muscular Christianity background excluded from covered_span. Relationship with 17-year-old Chata discussed but kept out of sexual-abuse/child-abuse as the story treats her age and circumstances as unclear. activist-organizer reflects MPA leadership and pro-war speeches.
